PMID:30952360.topic: Imaging for suspected occult scaphoid fracture
PMID:30952360.setting: UK-wide survey of 140 eligible acute NHS trusts (Warrington Hospital radiology department)

cycle1.result: 74 of 140 trusts responded (53%). 38 offered MRI first line for radiographically occult scaphoid injury (51% of trusts), 25 preferred CT and 11 repeat plain radiographs. Of the 38 offering MRI, 26 provided it within 1 week and the rest within 2 weeks.

PMID:30952360.other_findings: No significant relationship between the number of MRI scanners and provision of MRI or time to MRI; no trends by hospital size or location.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8574453.setting: South West London Elective Orthopaedic Centre, high-volume elective orthopaedic centre
EPMC:PMC:PMC8574453.standard: Local theatre protocols: team meeting to begin at 08:00

cycle1.dates: 2 weeks over 12 days of theatre sessions
cycle1.result: Average team brief start time 08:05; 17/18 (94%) of late starts due to surgeon/anaesthetist lateness.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8574453.intervention: Findings presented at Clinical Governance; changes to local protocols during the COVID-19 pandemic.

cycle2.result: Average team brief start time 08:08; 10/22 (45%) of late starts due to surgeon/anaesthetist lateness.

EPMC:PMC:PMC8574453.other_findings: Late starts led to further delays in sending for patients; extraneous factors were blamed for the later average start time in the second cycle.

PMID:16570890.standard: National Blood Users Group guidelines (haemovigilance nurse employed in compliance)

cycle1.result: 11% of patients undergoing primary TKA required post-operative transfusion.

PMID:16570890.intervention: Routine cross-matching stopped for primary TKA, a Haemovigilance Nurse was employed, and post-operative cell salvage introduced for patients with preoperative haemoglobin below 12 g/dl.

cycle2.result: 17 of 233 patients (7%) received allogeneic blood, average two units; no statistically significant difference from the first audit.

PMID:16570890.other_findings: 36% of patients given a cell saver did not collect enough blood for re-transfusion and 10% needed further allogeneic blood; pre-operative anaemia and older age predicted transfusion.

PMID:19864348.setting: Fracture Liaison Service, Addenbrooke's Hospital, Cambridge
PMID:19864348.standard: National guidance recommending treatment in the majority of postmenopausal women with a history of low trauma fracture

cycle1.result: Of 1641 women, 526 (31%) had a past low trauma fracture; only 27.6% of these were receiving bone protective therapy (bisphosphonate 89%) and 35.6% calcium and vitamin D. Only 45.1% of women aged 75 and over with a previous fracture were treated.

PMID:19864348.other_findings: Treatment rates were highest after previous spine (61.9%) and hip (49.3%) fracture; the wrist was the commonest previous fracture site.

PMID:17346409.topic: Fragility fracture osteoporosis referral from fracture clinic
PMID:17346409.setting: Fracture clinic, Department of Orthopaedics, East Surrey Hospital, Redhill
PMID:17346409.standard: British Orthopaedic Association 2003 guidelines on care of fragility fracture patients (secondary prevention of osteoporotic fractures)

cycle1.result: Only 5 of 38 patients who should have been assessed and investigated for osteoporosis were referred or offered referral.

PMID:17346409.intervention: Steps to improve awareness among orthopaedic staff and prompt referral.

cycle2.result: 23 of 43 patients referred or offered referral.

PMID:17346409.other_findings: Authors suggest automated referral systems may be needed to reach rates near 100%.

PMID:12974599.setting: Glasgow Royal Infirmary, major elective general, orthopaedic and vascular surgery

cycle1.result: Mean core temperature on arrival in recovery 35.5 degrees C (range 32.2-37.2, SD +/- 0.74).

PMID:12974599.intervention: Simple but consistently implemented changes in practice to prevent hypothermia (details not given in the supplied text).

cycle2.result: Mean core temperature on arrival in recovery 36.6 degrees C (33.6-38.2, +/- 0.72); difference reached significance.

PMID:12974599.other_findings: Authors concluded postoperative hypothermia in elective patients could largely be eradicated.

PMID:27362595.standard: ANZHFR Minimum Data Set and NICE hip fracture guidelines; national health target of ED admission within 6 hours

cycle1.result: 76% admitted from ED within 6 hours; 86% had surgery within 48 hours; 82% had rehabilitation by Older People's Health; bisphosphonates prescribed for 56%.

PMID:16718297.other_findings: Orthopaedic POSSUM allocated patients into risk groups, with more complications in higher-risk groups.

PMID:27896467.setting: Trauma Department, General and Teaching Hospital Celje

cycle1.result: 20% seen preoperatively by a physician or geriatrician; 93.1% had surgical repair, 58.5% of them within 48 h of admission.

EPMC:PPR:PPR827462.setting: Orthopaedic specialty ward of a teaching hospital in Dublin

cycle1.result: 11 (55%) patients wearing TEDS correctly; 13 (65%) educated on the importance of TEDS.

cycle1.result: Osteoporosis pharmacotherapy or hip protector use improved by 8.0% in the intervention group and 0.6% in controls (P=.72); no significant improvement in any quality indicator.

PMID:17904460.intervention: Audit and feedback, educational modules, teleconferences and academic detailing.
PMID:17904460.other_findings: Participation was low; completing the educational module (OR 4.8) and academic detailer contact (OR 4.5) were associated with prescribing.

PMID:24306164.setting: Three trauma centres in South Wales (Welsh Institute of Spinal Injuries, University Hospital of Wales)

cycle1.result: 29% received digital rectal examination; paralysis level not documented in 20.4%; MRC grade documented in only 24.5% though assessed in 73.5%; secondary survey after 2 h in 54.6%.

PMID:9814741.setting: Orthopaedic theatre, Palmerston North Hospital; subsequent 6-month post at a tertiary trauma centre

cycle1.result: Fluoroscopy used in 260 procedures, 124 min screening (0.48 min per procedure); lead aprons worn in 99% and thyroid guards in 32%; surgeon's hand in beam in 15%; calculated hand exposure under 5% of recommended levels.

PMID:26001993.topic: Foot orthoses prescription for flexible pes planus
PMID:26001993.setting: University of South Australia podiatry clinic

PMID:30705543.topic: Wound closure technique in knee arthroplasty
PMID:30705543.setting: P.D Hinduja Hospital and Medical Research Centre, Mumbai

cycle1.result: Mean Stony Brook Scar Evaluation Scale score 4.4 (SD 0.73, range 3-5).

PMID:25163959.standard: Royal College of Surgeons guidelines on operation notes

PMID:24928271.standard: EndoCert certification requirements for structural and process quality

cycle1.result: 172 nonconformities found in 23 pilot clinics.

PMID:24928271.other_findings: Long-term outcome effects to be analysed with the German endoprosthesis register (EPRD).

EPMC:PPR:PPR795407.standard: GMC, Royal College of Surgeons Glasgow and British Orthopaedic Association guidance on consent

cycle1.result: Abbreviations used in 54% of consent forms.

cycle2.result: Abbreviations used in 22% of consent forms.

PMID:15866830.setting: National Hospital Discharge Survey data (St. Luke's Hospital, Bethlehem, PA)

cycle1.result: Keller arthroplasty patients more likely to have diabetes (OR 4.00), diabetic neuropathy (OR 3.80), foot wound or ulcer (OR 2.62) and osteomyelitis (OR 2.65).
